doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Al Hibbler and how he judged women by their walk
summary: Jeannie recalls blind singer Al Hibbler winning bets by telling ugly women from pretty ones by their walk, and telling a Cadillac by its paint.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And “Trees.” [sings] “I think that I shall never see/A poem lovely as a tree.” Yeah that was a blind man. That was his thing. Because I played for Al. Yeah, Al Hibbler. And he would hang out at this night club after we got through playing the show, and it was called Benny Rivers. And he’d tell all the guys, and they’d have bets, and money was passing along, and he says, “All right Al, what’s coming now?” He said he could tell an ugly woman or a pretty one. He’s blind you know, right? And so now they didn’t know how he was figuring that out. And so he’d listen, and say, “That’s an ugly one.” They’d say okay, and give him the money. “Here come a pretty one.” “Oh, this one is gorgeous.” And he’d say, “You sure you can’t see?” He said no, he could tell the way they walk. He said ugly people dragged their feet. And he would win all their money. They never did figure out how he did it.
Well the attitude and the sound.
The attitude and the sound, see the sound.
From the sound and the way—
See ugly women he said ugly women dragged their feet.
That’s right. And they walked on the heels on the back of their shoes.

And that really made me be aware — I said this guy made more money than he made on the gig. He was a funny guy. He says, “I can tell a Cadillac.” He’d put his hand on it, and he could feel the paint. He could tell the different paint. He could tell the difference between a Cadillac and a Ford. I saw this with my own eyes.
